# Cleanup Recovery Safety Checklist: Spec Archive and Evidence Retention

**Purpose**: Validate SPEC-002A cleanup and recovery requirements before task generation, with focus on active-spec removal safety, raw artifact recovery, dry-run provenance boundaries, unsafe checkout behavior, current-target exclusion, and non-mutating post-merge cleanup.
**Created**: 2026-04-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` workflow from SPEC-002A source artifacts, the Archive Sweep command contract, Mission Control constitution principles, Git revision documentation, and GitHub Actions artifact-retention documentation.

## Active-Spec Cleanup Eligibility

- [x] CHK001 Does the specification require completed spec folders to remain in active `specs/**` until archive success is recorded? [Completeness, Spec FR-006]
- [x] CHK002 Does the specification require merge/tree references before completed spec folders may leave active `specs/**`? [Completeness, Spec FR-006, FR-015]
- [x] CHK003 Does the cleanup model require concrete recovery commands before removal from active `specs/**` is allowed? [Clarity, Spec FR-005, FR-006]
- [x] CHK004 Are cleanup decisions framed as explicit and reviewable rather than automatic deletion? [Consistency, Spec FR-010, Plan §Non-Goals]

## Recovery Evidence and Raw Artifact Access

- [x] CHK005 Does the specification require durable traceability from archive records back to source spec paths, PR URL, merge commit, CI run, and recovery commands? [Completeness, Spec FR-005]
- [x] CHK006 Is at least one concrete raw-artifact recovery command format specified, such as `git show <merge-sha>:specs/<feature>/spec.md`? [Clarity, Spec FR-005]
- [x] CHK007 Does the data model define `recoveryCommands` as part of the Archive Report rather than leaving recovery as an external operator assumption? [Completeness, Data Model §ArchiveReport]
- [x] CHK008 Can SC-006 be objectively evaluated by using a recorded merge/tree reference and `git show` command to recover a removed active-spec file? [Measurability, Spec SC-006]

## Dry-Run Evidence Boundaries

- [x] CHK009 Does the Archive Sweep output requirement record cleanup mode and whether cleanup is safe to apply? [Completeness, Spec FR-017]
- [x] CHK010 Does the specification state that current Archive Sweep dry-run evidence for SPEC-001 and SPEC-002 is provenance evidence only, not permission to remove active spec folders? [Gap resolved, Spec FR-021]
- [x] CHK011 Does the plan record that the current dirty/non-safe checkout keeps cleanup-sensitive archive behavior dry-run only? [Consistency, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Gate Evaluation]
- [x] CHK012 Does the quickstart require branch and worktree safety checks before apply-mode cleanup? [Coverage, Quickstart §Safety Checks]

## Branch Safety and Target Exclusion

- [x] CHK013 Does the specification require unsafe base branch or dirty worktree conditions to force dry-run or stop behavior? [Completeness, Spec FR-009]
- [x] CHK014 Does the Archive Sweep contract require dry-run by default when the branch is unsafe or the worktree is dirty? [Consistency, Contract §Archive Sweep Command Contract]
- [x] CHK015 Does the specification exclude the current target spec from cleanup eligibility during the same autopilot run that selected it? [Clarity, Spec FR-007, FR-008]
- [x] CHK016 Does the specification state that SPEC-002A becomes eligible only after it merges and a later Archive Sweep sees it as merged? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, FR-007]

## History and Post-Merge Mutation Safety

- [x] CHK017 Does the specification prohibit cleanup that rewrites git history or depends on post-merge CI silently mutating `main`? [Gap resolved, Spec FR-020]
- [x] CHK018 Does the source workflow itself define the non-rewrite and no-silent-post-merge-CI cleanup constraints that SPEC-002A artifacts should preserve? [Traceability, Workflow §Guardrails]

## Notes

- Initial run status: two cleanup-recovery-safety requirement-writing gaps found in CHK010 and CHK017.
- Research sources: Git revision syntax supports `rev:path` blob/tree recovery from committed history; Git history documentation treats history rewriting as a distinct operation class; GitHub Actions artifacts and logs have retention limits, so durable cleanup evidence cannot rely only on mutable or expiring CI artifacts.

## Remediation Re-run

- [x] CHK019 Was the dry-run provenance gap resolved by stating that SPEC-001/SPEC-002 dry-run evidence is not cleanup permission unless a later clean safe apply-mode run records archive success, merge/tree references, recovery commands, and safe-to-apply cleanup state? [Resolved, Spec FR-021; Plan §Technical Context; Data Model §ArchiveSweepRun; Quickstart §Dry-Run Archive Validation; Contract §Archive Sweep Command Contract]
- [x] CHK020 Was the history/post-merge mutation gap resolved by prohibiting history rewrite and silent post-merge CI mutation for active-spec cleanup? [Resolved, Spec FR-020; Plan §Non-Goals; Quickstart §Safety Checks; Contract §Archive Sweep Command Contract]
- [x] CHK021 Does SC-001 now make dry-run evidence explicitly non-authorizing for cleanup? [Resolved, Spec SC-001]
- [x] CHK022 Does SC-006 now require recovery through recorded merge/tree references and `git show` while preserving reviewed forward cleanup history? [Resolved, Spec SC-006]
- [x] CHK023 Does the data model now distinguish `dryRunProvenanceOnly` and cleanup permission state from apply-mode cleanup? [Resolved, Data Model §ArchiveReport, §ArchiveSweepRun]
- [x] CHK024 Does the quickstart now require checking that cleanup is reviewed, forward-only, and not performed by post-merge CI mutation? [Resolved, Quickstart §Safety Checks]
